dedupe_keys.name: cosimulationengine distributed modular co simulation engine for building systems

description: COsimulationEngine is the code of a distributed modular co-simulation engine released by the Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics IBP in Nürnberg, with Georg Ferdinand Schneider as project lead and Viet-Tung Hoang as lead developer. Its Python backend uses aiohttp, requests and SQLite, and its dependencies include fmpy for Functional Mock-up Units, pyads for Beckhoff ADS controllers and xknx for KNX building automation, which points to coupling simulation models with real building control hardware; a front end is built with NPM. Parts of the work were funded through the Mittelstand 4.0 initiative of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy. Coverage: generic technical building systems, not tied to a place. Access: source on GitHub and the initial pre-release v0.0.1 archived on Zenodo on 2019-04-29. Licence: Apache 2.0 according to the README (Zenodo lists 'other open'); free. Caveats: this is an early pre-release with a short README and no documentation of models or examples, and no later release was seen. Simulation uses are hardware-in-the-loop and co-simulation of building automation, controls and simulation models, as a basis for building digital twins. Related records: the HELICS platform and the PyEPlus co-simulation records.
